classification.difficultyReason: A supplied vector identity guides the midpoint proof before a dot-product check and geometric conclusion.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Show that the diagonals $PR$ and $QS$ bisect each other by showing $\tfrac12\overrightarrow{PR}=\overrightarrow{PQ}+\tfrac12\overrightarrow{QS}$.

answer.short: $\tfrac12\overrightarrow{PR}=\overrightarrow{PQ}+\tfrac12\overrightarrow{QS}=\left(\tfrac{15}{2},\tfrac{15}{2}\right)$, so the diagonals have the same midpoint.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\overrightarrow{PR}&=(7-(-8),18-3)=(15,15),\\\tfrac12\overrightarrow{PR}&=\left(\tfrac{15}{2},\tfrac{15}{2}\right),\\\overrightarrow{PQ}&=(3-(-8),7-3)=(11,4),\\\overrightarrow{QS}&=(-4-3,14-7)=(-7,7),\\\tfrac12\overrightarrow{QS}&=\left(-\tfrac72,\tfrac72\right),\\\overrightarrow{PQ}+\tfrac12\overrightarrow{QS}&=\left(11-\tfrac72,4+\tfrac72\right)\\\overrightarrow{PQ}+\tfrac12\overrightarrow{QS}&=\left(\tfrac{15}{2},\tfrac{15}{2}\right)=\tfrac12\overrightarrow{PR}.\end{align*}$$

Both expressions locate the same point from $P$: the midpoint of $PR$ and the midpoint of $QS$. Hence the diagonals bisect each other.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Show that the diagonals are perpendicular by showing that $\overrightarrow{PR}\cdot\overrightarrow{QS}=0$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: What type of special quadrilateral is $PQRS$? Give reasons for your answer.

answer.short: Rhombus: its diagonals bisect each other at $90^\circ$.
answer.worked: The diagonals bisect each other, so $PQRS$ is a parallelogram. Its diagonals are also perpendicular, so $PQRS$ is a rhombus.
